author: Caroline Davies
description:
Some in UK’s security services questioned why Welsh Labour firebrand was of interest

Aneurin “Nye” Bevan, the Welsh Labour firebrand who spearheaded the creation of the NHS, was monitored by security services for more than two decades, though his personal file was “remarkably tame”, according to official files released to the public.

Bevan came to MI5’s attention in the 1930s over concerns about his links with known communists, papers released to the National Archives show. Monitoring continued even after he became a minister in the postwar Labour government that created the NHS.

Continue reading...
title: Aneurin Bevan’s personal security file was ‘remarkably tame’ – National Archives

author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
description:
Committee cites shortfalls of submarines and warships and says ‘dramatic progress’ needed by end of decade

Britain risks failing to deter future Russian aggression in the high north beyond the UK because of shortfalls in the number and availability of Royal Navy submarines and warships, MPs on the defence select committee have said.

The committee focused on the slow deployment of HMS Dragon to Cyprus this spring, declining numbers of frigates, and reports that all five Astute-class attack submarines were in dock this summer as evidence of a navy under-resourced for the threat.

Continue reading...
title: Royal Navy lacks resources to counter Russian threat in high north, MPs warn

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Former speaker is latest target of mailings sent to various Congress members in the lead-up to the midterm elections

California representative Nancy Pelosi’s office received “a suspicious letter” on Wednesday in what appears to be the latest incident of ill-intentioned mailings targeted at US Congress members before the midterm elections.

The offices of more than three dozen members of Congress across the political spectrum have received envelopes containing white powder in recent days. One lawmaker’s office said preliminary tests indicated the powder was not hazardous.

Continue reading...
title: Nancy Pelosi’s office latest recipient of letter containing white powder

author: Maanvi Singh, José Olivares and Sam Levin
description:
With ICE arrests and detentions at their highest levels, immigration remains a key issue for voters less than two weeks before election day

  • Sign in or sign up to join the conversation

  • From mass raids to quiet crackdown: a timeline of Trump’s strategic ICE pivot

It’s our last US midterms live Q&A before election day on 3 November, and our reporters are answering your immigration questions.

Since Donald Trump began his second term, ICE arrests have reached record levels, operations have become
title: How will Trump’s mass deportation agenda shape the US midterm elections? Our reporters answer your questions

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
House prices in Sydney are at a two-year low after falling 4.7% in the September quarter, to $1.66m according to Domain report

House prices are falling across every capital city for the first time in 15 years and the second time on record, according to figures from Domain’s September Quarter 2026 House Price Report.

House prices in Sydney are at a two-year low after falling 4.7% in the September quarter, to $1.66 million.

Continue reading...
title: House prices falling in every Australian capital city for first time in 15 years

author: Penry Buckley
description:
The south-west metro extension will open on Friday 30 October, more than two years after the former T3 heavy rail line closed

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A long-awaited extension to Sydney’s metro line will open on Friday next week, bringing an end to more than two years of replacement buses for residents in the city’s south-west.

In a video shared on Instagram on Thursday morning, the New South Wales premier, Chris Minns, announced that the south-west metro extension would open on Friday 30 October. In a statement, the government said the first service would commence at 4.31am.

Continu
title: ‘Huge moment’: long-awaited extension to Sydney’s metro line to open next week

author: Nino Bucci
description:
Australia-first laws provide a third legal option other than burial and cremation for the treatment of bodies

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Several New South Wales MPs say they want their own bodies turned into “human compost” after Australian-first laws were passed allowing the unusual practice.

The laws, passed on Wednesday, provide a third legal option other than burial and cremation for the treatment of bodies.

Continue reading...
title: NSW passes ‘human compost’ laws with several MPs saying they will utilise practice after they die

author: Ariana Baio in New York
description:
Incumbent Mike Lawler is fending off a challenge from Democrat Cait Conley in state’s 17th congressional district

  • US politics live – latest updates

Elon Musk’s Super Pac has spent more than $500,000 in New York’s highly competitive 17th congressional district race to help Mike Lawler, the Republican incumbent, hold on to his seat.

Lawler, a moderate Republican, is fending off a challenge from Democrat Cait Conley in the Hudson valley. It is among the most-watched races that could determine whether Republic
title: Elon Musk’s Super Pac spends $500,000 to back New York Republican in midterms

author: Ben Quinn and Henry Dyer
description:
Jack Ross was filmed allegedly discussing with an undercover reporter violent options to deal with enemies

A former Conservative election candidate has been suspended from the party after he was seemingly filmed discussing the cost of hiring contract killers and offering to “broker” the services of a far-right activist with alleged paramilitary links.

Jack Ross was filmed apparently asking an undercover reporter “What do you want done?” before listing the type of violent options that could be bought.

Continue reading...
title: Former Tory election candidate suspended over contract killing claims

author: Anna Betts
description:
New Mexico lawsuit claims ‘in exchange for furthering Epstein’s criminal project, his associates received generous salaries’

The attorney general of New Mexico on Wednesday filed a civil lawsuit against Jeffrey Epstein’s longtime attorney, Darren Indyke, and Epstein’s longtime accountant, Richard Kahn, accusing them of having “facilitated and concealed” Epstein’s crimes, and is seeking to stop them from being paid by Epstein’s estate while the litigation plays out.

The lawsuit, filed in the US district court for the district of New Mexico, names Kahn and Indyke as defendants both in their individual capacity, and in their capacity as co-executors of Epstein’s estate. The complaint also names the Epstein’s estate, and the 1953 Trust, which holds the estate’s assets.

Continue reading...
title: Epstein’s attorney and accountant accused of ‘facilitating and concealing’ his crimes in lawsuit

author: Julian Borger and Quique Kierszenbaumin Petah Tikva
description:
US photojournalist describes ‘protective shield’, vows to return to work in West Bank and criticises Netanyahu comments on incident

The Washington Post photojournalist who was attacked and seriously injured by Israeli settlers on the West Bank on Friday has described how she was saved with the help of local Palestinians.

Heidi Levine sustained four fractured vertebrae, two broken ribs and four puncture wounds when she was knocked to the ground and repeatedly beaten by a crowd of masked settlers while she and other journalists were covering the olive harvest in the Palestinian village of Abu Falah, north of Ramallah.

Continue reading...
title: Heidi Levine recounts how Palestinian youths helped save her in settler attack

author: Andrew Roth in Kharkiv
description:
Steve Witkoff’s flattery of the Russian leader could be just the start of a mendacious stratagem from a US president who says Moscow ‘has been fine on Ukraine’

They say the first casualty of war is truth. For the Trump administration, the road to peace with Russia now encompasses some extraordinary lies.

Steve Witkoff delivered one as he sat down with Vladimir Putin in his native St Petersburg on Wednesday, aiming to close the deal on Russia’s land grab in Ukraine with the White House’s strategy of maximum pressure on Kyiv and saccharine flattery of the Kremlin.

Continue reading...
title: ‘You are a humanitarian also, sir’: the US feeds Putin with lies as Ukraine’s children take cover and die | Andrew Roth

author: Auzzy Byrdsell
description:
Officials say the explosion released an airborne irritant that can cause burning of the eyes, nose, mouth and skin

Officials are investigating a tank explosion in Toledo, Ohio, that released a chemical into the air, causing a mass evacuation in the area.

One person, a first responder, was injured and taken to the hospital, but officials believe the injuries are non-life-threatening. They are also unsure about the cause of the explosion.

Continue reading...
title: Chemical tank explosion in Toledo, Ohio, prompts mass evacuation

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Wedgewood Polls said project was designed to highlight lack of scrutiny over polling sector by mainstream media

A polling firm has admitted to using fabricated data in surveys that were picked up by national media outlets in the US, claiming the project was a “social experiment” designed to expose the lack of scrutiny over the sector.

Wedgewood Polls released a statement on Tuesday on social media, after the polling and election analysis site FiftyPlusOne reached out for comment on an investigation it had conducted into their surveys and data.

Continue reading...
title: Pollster admits to fabricating data for ‘social experiment’ to expose flaws of industry

author: Maya Yang
description:
Jaden J Read was arrested after federal authorities say he posted threats online before president’s Wichita rally

A 24-year-old Kansas man has been arrested for allegedly threatening to shoot Donald Trump.

Authorities arrested Jaden J Read, of Clearwater, Kansas, last Saturday after he allegedly posted threats to kill the US president at his rally in the Wichita area on Monday, according to the justice department.

Continue reading...
title: 24-year-old Kansas man arrested for allegedly threatening to shoot Donald Trump

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Republican Neil Bush says he was ‘deeply troubled’ by Ken Paxton’s conduct and ‘enormously impressed’ with Talarico

  • US politics live – latest updates

Neil Bush, a son of former president George HW Bush and a lifelong Republican, announced on Tuesday that he crossed party lines to vote for James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Texas.

In a Facebook post, Neil Bush said he chose to vote early for Talarico over Ken Paxton, the Republican candidate and current Texas attorney general, because he was “deeply troubled” by Paxton’s conduct and was “enormously impressed” by Talarico’s principles.
title: Bush’s brother crosses party lines to vote for James Talarico for Senate

author: Jon Henley in Paris
description:
French president criticises leaders for spreading misleading information as country prepares for further protests this weekend

  • Europe live – latest updates

Emmanuel Macron has accused Donald Trump and other foreign leaders of making “stupid comments” about France’s street unrest for political gain, as the country prepared for more protests this weekend.

Speaking during a visit to Qatar, the French president did not name names but said “manipulation of information” after Saturday’s riots had led to “comments that are as unacceptable as they are stupid, from many people, including foreign leaders”.
title: Macron accuses Trump and other foreign leaders of making ‘stupid comments’ about France unrest

author: Jon Henley and Guardian correspondents
description:
Nationalist leaders are framing unrest as consequence of failed liberal governance and open borders

Europe’s far-right leaders have jumped on the violence that rocked numerous cities last weekend, framing it as the inevitable consequence of failed liberal governance and open-border policies and insisting only they can restore law and order.

Months away from key elections in Spain, France and Italy, authoritarian nationalists are eager to weaponise the wave of street unrest, originating in peaceful protests over the cost of living and deteriorating public services but hijacked by violent rioters.

Continue reading...
title: Europe’s far right seizes on protest violence to push authoritarian anti-immigration agenda

author: Jennifer Rankin Brussels correspondent
description:
As US support ebbs away, looming European elections and growing financial strains across the continent could fracture the precious coalition that has kept Ukraine afloat

Europe woke up last Friday to another belligerent outburst from Donald Trump – this time berating Ukraine’s wartime leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy again. Just a few days after his diesel deal with the Kremlin, the US president said Zelenskyy was more difficult to deal with than Vladimir Putin and blamed Ukraine’s leader for rocketing oil prices – without any reference to the impact of his own war on Iran.

The contrast in Europe was obvious. When Zelenskyy walked into the multi-coloured summit room of the European Council headquarters in Brussels that Friday morning, the EU’s 27 leaders burst into applause, getting to their feet to offer big hugs and brisk handshakes. Eu
title: ​Europe stands by Ukraine – but how long can that last?

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Voters disapprove of Trump’s handling of economy and cost of living, says poll in new low recorded by NY Times/Siena

Donald Trump’s approval rating sank to 36% just two weeks before the midterm elections, the lowest recorded in a poll by the New York Times/Siena College, with most respondents expressing frustration over his handling of the US economy, cost of living and Iran war.

In an October survey of approximately 3,494 likely voters, 59% said they disapproved of Trump’s handling of his job, and 52% said they planned to vote for the Democratic candidate in the upcoming election.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s approval rating drops to 36% two weeks before midterms, poll finds

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Water, gas and fresh food running out in Taiz as fighting intensifies and Houthi advance cuts off most supply routes

The humanitarian crisis in the besieged Yemeni city of Taiz is becoming unmanageable as the city runs out of water, gas and fresh food, Oxfam aid workers in the country have warned.

Iran-allied Houthi forces have largely encircled the city of more than 900,000 people, cutting it off from most supply routes. This week, heavy fighting has raged around the city’s old airport, causing extensive damage in a densely populated residential area.

Continue reading...
title: Besieged Yemeni city on verge of ‘unmanageable’ crisis, aid workers warn

author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
description:
Former art teacher, who cared for her disabled son, ‘received almost no support’, said her local MP Manuela Perteghella

Andy Burnham has backed mandatory suicide prevention training for social workers after the “devastating” death of Matilda Davis, a parent-carer who killed herself minutes after meeting professionals.

The Guardian revealed in August how the “absolutely inspirational” 36-year-old had taken her life after feeling “completely exhausted” and failed by England’s social care system.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham backs mandatory suicide prevention training for social workers after Matilda Davis’s death

author: Josh Butler and Krishani Dhanji
description:
Home and office safety a common concern in Australian federal police and Asio safety briefings with politicians following alleged attack on MP Helen Haines

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Security agencies will review safety precautions for MPs’ homes and offices after numerous federal politicians told police and Asio in safety briefings that they were worried about widening threats after the alleged attack on Helen Haines.

The Labor government and politicians across the parliament are still considering how they will respond when they return to Canberra next week, with ideas being floated including a new committee on MPs’ safety, greater resources for police, and motions of condolence for Haines,
title: Australian politicians say they are paying thousands for their own security upgrades amid rising threats

author: Jack Larkin
description:
Peak body for immunologists changes guidelines as evidence shows up to 90% of those reporting allergy don’t have one

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The majority of Australians who report a penicillin allergy are not truly allergic, prompting the peak body for immunologists to change its guidelines in a bid to reduce hospitals stays and tackle antimicrobial resistance.

Penicillin, one of the most commonly prescribed antibiotics in Australia, was thought to cause allergies in 10% of Australians, or about 2.8 million people.

Continue reading...
title: Majority of Australians who report penicillin allergy not truly allergic

author: Anna Betts
description:
Liberal justice says recent decisions on redistricting and campaign finance have undermined democracy and polarized US even more

  • US politics live – latest updates

Elena Kagan criticized rulings made by the US supreme court’s conservative majority this week, arguing that its recent decisions on redistricting and campaign finance had undermined America’s democracy.

“The court has kind of blinded itself to the very deleterious effects of their rulings on how the political system works,” said Kagan, one of the court’s three liberal justices, during a discussion at Catholic University’s law school in Washington DC on Tuesday, according to multiple reports.
title: Kagan says supreme court conservatives have made US political system ‘a nightmare’

author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
description:
Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail

Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.

Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities in south Florida.

Continue reading...
title: Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
SEIU Local 1000, representing nurses and teachers, pushing for higher wages, telework and affordable healthcare

Thousands of California state workers were set to strike on Wednesday, rallying outside government buildings in several cities, as tensions boiled over lapsed contract negotiations with Governor Gavin Newsom’s administration.

SEIU Local 1000, a union that represents roughly 100,000 public employees, including nurses and teachers, has been pushing for higher wages, flexible telework and affordable healthcare.

Continue reading...
title: Thousands of California public employees set to strike over contract

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Pippa Boardman said she lost her dignity through data breach at Royal Cornwall hospital by man she barely knew

A woman was told she had cancer by a hospital employee she barely knew who had accessed her medical records days before she was due to receive test results from her consultant.

Pippa Boardman said she lost her dignity and privacy through the data breach at the Royal Cornwall hospital in Truro.

Continue reading...
title: Woman told she had cancer by NHS worker who inappropriately accessed her records

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Zack Coughlan, 23, killed Jamie Collins, 21, in garden of home they shared and initially denied murder

A university student who lay in wait for his housemate to return home before stabbing him 30 times has been jailed for life with a minimum term of 28 years.

Zack Coughlan, 23, dressed in black and wore a mask and gloves to ambush Jamie Collins, 21, in the garden of their home in Filton, South Gloucestershire.

Continue reading...
title: Student who stabbed housemate to death in Gloucestershire jailed for life

author: Peter Stone
description:
Coordination by Democratic officials overseeing elections includes Zoom calls and in-person tabletop exercises

Democratic state attorneys general, other top state officials and civic groups have accelerated planning to thwart any federal meddling in the November midterm elections by Donald Trump as he continues his false charges of widespread voting fraud and veiled threats of interfering in the process.

Since early this year, 24 Democratic attorneys general have expanded coordination with about a dozen Democratic secretaries of state and several civic groups using weekly Zoom calls and in-person tabletop exercises to strategize about countering any federal intervention in the elections.

Continue reading...
title: State attorneys general step up plans to counter Trump’s meddling in midterms

author: Pjotr Sauer
description:
Russia unilaterally frees Stephen Hubbard after US request while Steve Witkoff praises Putin as a ‘humanitarian’

  • Europe live – latest updates

  • US politics live – latest updates

Vladimir Putin ordered the release of an American from a Russian jail as he met Donald Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday for fresh talks on ending the war in Ukraine, amid increasingly close relations between Moscow and Washington.

Trump had previously asked Putin to free Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old former teacher who had spent more than four years in Russian jails on
title: Putin orders release of jailed American as he meets Trump envoy for Ukraine talks

author: Martin Belam
description:
Billionaire Michael Bloomberg is spending $80m to help Democratic candidates, while Trump has promised Republicans $400m. Plus a vital investigation into justice in Louisiana

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Vast sums of money are being ploughed into November’s midterms, with the billionaire Michael Bloomberg spending $80m to help Democratic candidates, and Donald Trump announcing he intends to spend $400m to aid Republican candidates, with $300m already disbursed.

Bloomberg made the contributions in September and October, particularly focused on Democrats running to flip the US House of Representatives. Democrats believe they are favored to take back the House, though they’
title: Race for crucial midterms attracting vast sums of money on both sides | First Thing

author: Rokhaya Diallo, Alexander Hurst, Michael Hubbard and Guardian moderators
description:
At 3pm BST / 4pm CEST Friday 23 Oct, Guardian Europe columnists Rokhaya Diallo and Alexander Hurst will be live taking questions from our readers about the riots and protests in France. Send your questions by email now to conversations@theguardian.com, or join the discussion on Friday

After weeks of protests and a weekend of riots in which a town hall was set ablaze, 2,000-plus shops were looted, 2,300 people were arrested and 1,000 police injured, the repercussions for France – for its society and its economy – continue. Allegations of police brutality surfaced, and the violent protests unnerved investors, resulting in a debt sell-off, with borrowing costs rising higher than for Greece. All of this ahead of a hotly contested presidential election that’s now just six mo
title: Reader Q&A: What’s next for France after a weekend of riots? Ask our Europe columnists

author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
description:
Water company, Environment Agency and local campaigners say 12-mile tunnel could take sewage away from England’s largest lake

Plans are under way for a new giant tunnel to transport sewage away from Windermere, England’s largest lake.

Windermere, in the Lake District, has suffered from widespread raw sewage and bacterial pollution driven by discharges from United Utilities. Campaigners say this pollution has caused more frequent toxic blue-green algal blooms, with the public advised to avoid swimming in the lake.

Continue reading...
title: Giant tunnel proposed to tackle Windermere sewage discharges

author: Frances Mao
description:
President’s social media post says sites should pay the communities where they will be located and comes amid growing unpopularity of facilities

Sign up for Breaking News US email

Good morning and welcome to our coverage of US politics. With 14 days until the mid-terms, we’re heading into the final straight.

President Donald Trump attended a rally last night in North Carolina, where Democrat Roy Cooper is leading Trump’s pick Michael Whatley by a considerable margin.
title: Trump calls for data center ‘dividends’ in bid to win over midterm voters – US politics live

author: Matthew Weaver and Rowena Mason
description:
Miatta Fahnbulleh avoids explicitly expressing support for longer path to permanent residency for foreign workers

  • UK politics live – latest updates

A cabinet split over Shabana Mahmood’s immigration policy has deepened after the energy secretary refused to say she backed plans to make foreign workers wait 15 years to claim permanent residency in the UK.

Miatta Fahnbulleh said in an interview with Sky News that changes to the immigration system were needed and that they should be “based on the principle of compassion” and recognising contribution.

Continue reading...
title: Cabinet split widens as minister refuses to back Shabana Mahmood 15-year policy

author: Patrick Greenfield
description:
Few believe decision will bring back city’s boom years, but workers hope it will keep as many North Sea jobs for now

  • UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea

  • What does the UK’s approval of the Jackdaw gasfield mean?

As recently as 2012, Aberdeen boasted the highest concentration of millionaires in the UK. An ATM reportedly had the highest withdrawal rate in Europe in the 90s, as oil and gas wealth flowed through the city. House prices skyrocketed in the scramble for space as fossil fuel firms transformed
title: ‘Jackdaw means we pay our mortgages’: relief in Aberdeen over gasfield approval

author: Ashifa Kassam European community affairs correspondent
description:
Hamstrung governments seem to have no answer to the public’s furious demands, making further discontent likely

  • Europe live – latest updates

In France, it was the piles of wheelie bins stacked up against school entrances that first hinted at the scale of student anger over crumbling classrooms and teacher shortages. In Spain, it was a tent camp that steadily grew in the heart of the capital as residents railed against soaring housing costs.

Similar scenes have since sprung up in Belgium, Italy and Portugal, and clashes have convulsed Albania’s capital of Tirana, hinting at an autumn of protests across Europe.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A powerful warning’: will Europe’s angry protests lead to real political change?

author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
description:
Critics say move will jeopardise climate targets, fail to cut cost of living and distract from need to decarbonise energy

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Climate campaigners and green experts have condemned the government’s decision to allow the drilling of the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea.

They said approval for the site would jeopardise the UK’s climate targets, fail to reduce the cost of living, and distract from the need to decarbonise the
title: Climate campaigners condemn ‘maddening’ decision to approve Jackdaw gasfield

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
The Jackdaw field will start supplying gas to homes and businesses from the end of the month, the government said

UK inflation climbed by more than expected in September to 3.5% after a surge in prices from the conflict in the Middle East that has pushed up the cost of diesel to record levels, Phillip Inman reports.

Here is the official Jackdaw decision.

Continue reading...
title: Labour accused of ‘climate vandalism’ by Green leader Polanski after Jackdaw gasfield approved – UK politics live

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
The meeting comes after the US official held ‘constructive’ talks with Zelenskyy in Norway

Meanwhile, Ukraine’s ⁠anti-corruption police said ⁠that ⁠detectives were ​searching the premises of ⁠the National Bank of Ukraine ⁠and also ​the ‌home address of ‌one of ‌the central bank’s employees, Reuters reported.

The anti-corruption police said in a statement ‌on the Telegram app that ​no one has been detained or issued ⁠a suspicion notice. ​The central ​bank did ​not immediately ​respond ‌to ​a request ​for comment.

Continue reading...
title: US envoy Witkoff lands in Russia for talks with Vladimir Putin about Ukraine – Europe live

author: Josh Butler
description:
Independent senator’s goals ‘much bigger’ than prime ministership, he reveals in first speech to national press club

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

He’s six foot tall and full of muscle, but David Pocock’s real strength is often sounding like the most sensible, commonsense voice in the room.

At his first speech to the national press club on Wednesday, he said he wasn’t launching a bid for prime minister – no matter how much some people might like the softly spoken senator to have more say in federal politics.

A 25% tax on gas exports, which he said could fund anything from boosting welfare to health reforms and aged care.

A 5% levy on datacentres to capture more benefits from the AI boom.

Transpare
title: Soft-spoken David Pocock has big ambitions – but first he wants politicians to ‘double down’ on kindness

author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
description:
Government paid £10.9bn in debt interest, the highest September figure since records began

  • Business live – latest updates

The Treasury ran a higher than expected budget deficit of £24.5bn last month as rising inflation pushed up the interest paid on government debt, increasing pressure on John Healey before his first budget next Wednesday.

Official figures show the government paid £10.9bn in debt interest: the highest September figure since records began, and only the eighth time the monthly number has been above £10bn.

Continue reading...
title: UK government borrowing rises to £24.5bn as John Healey prepares for budget

author: Tess Ikonomou
description:
Children as young as 12 among dozens subject to federal police operations since 2020, parliamentary inquiry hears

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia is facing a “tsunami” of youth crime as artificial intelligence accelerates the pace and scale of radicalisation, a parliamentary inquiry has heard.

The Australian federal police acting deputy commissioner Sandra Booth told the hearing on Wednesday that, while radicalisation had traditionally taken years or months, that process could now happen within days.

Continue reading...
title: AFP warns Australia of ‘tsunami of youth crime’ and radicalisation accelerated by AI

author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter
description:
NextDC tells investors plans to double the size of its west Melbourne datacentre have hit obstacle after community objects to 22 metres-high power poles

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s largest datacentre operator has been forced to delay the controversial expansion of its M3 site in Melbourne’s west amid a pause in construction of new 22m power poles following community protest.

On Wednesday, NextDC told the Australian Stock Exchange that delays to electricity provider Jemena’s upgrade of the power poles – essential to delivering the increased electricity required by the expanded West Footscray site – would mean the expansion would be pushed back to the 2027/2028 financial year.
title: Australia’s largest datacentre operator NextDC’s shares dive as Melbourne expansion delayed

author: Kat Wong
description:
Friend of accused double murderer tells supreme court that van had lemony smell and blue tarp in back before Bunnings stop

Beau Lamarre-Condon played Taylor Swift’s song No Body, No Crime while attempting to dispose of two corpses, a court has heard.

The NSW supreme court has been told he was driving to Bungonia with a friend when the song was played in the van.

Continue reading...
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon allegedly played Taylor Swift’s No Body, No Crime during body disposal, court told

author: Catie McLeod
description:
Ghanda and Windsor Smith are among lowest-rated in Baptist World Aid ethical fashion report based on metrics such as wages and sustainability

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Online fast-fashion giant Shein is outperforming many Australian high street retailers on ethical standards, according to an industry review.

The 11th Baptist World Aid ethical fashion report, released on Tuesday, assessed the ethical practices of 138 Australian and international companies, representing 543 fashion brands.

Continue reading...
title: Fast-fashion giant Shein outperforms several Australian retailers on ethics, report says

author: Sian Cain
description:
Morgan Carey sued his sister over claims in her 2020 memoir, The Meaning of Mariah Carey, which he said falsely portrayed him as a violent drug dealer

A judge has dismissed a lawsuit from Mariah Carey’s brother, five years after he accused her of defaming him in her 2020 memoir, The Meaning of Mariah Carey.

In the memoir, Carey described Morgan as a “sometimes drug dealing, been-in-the-system, drunk-ass brother” and called him her “ex-brother”.

Continue reading...
title: Mariah Carey wins dismissal of brother’s defamation lawsuit over her memoir
